description:
Found while fixing bd-pl2 / GH#21. Deliberately left alone there because it is a
BEHAVIOUR change, not a message change, and would invert an existing test.

The finding: `detect_clock_skew(now_ms, reference_ms)` compares the local wall
clock against `WriteStamp::wall_ms` — which is wall-clock-AT-WRITE-TIME. So a
positive delta is just THE AGE OF THE NEWEST WRITE. `CLOCK_SKEW_WARN_MS` is 5
minutes (crates/kopi-beans/src/daemon/runtime/core/helpers.rs). Meaning: any
store nobody wrote to for 5 minutes warns about clock skew ON A PERFECTLY
CORRECT CLOCK.

That is exactly what GH#21's reporter hit. Their +61 min was consistent with
"nobody wrote for 61 minutes", NOT with their (genuinely) unsynced NTP. We sent
them chasing a clock problem that was not there. Aiyo.

The NEGATIVE branch is the real signal — a future-dated stamp cannot be
explained by an idle store.

Options:
  1. Warn only on negative delta. Cheapest, kills the false positive dead, but
     gives up on detecting a locally-fast clock (which DOES matter — see below).
  2. Compare against a second clock source (remote HEAD commit time, peer stamp
     during replication) so there is a real second opinion.
  3. Keep positive warnings but require corroboration — e.g. only warn positive
     when a write has landed recently, so "ahead" cannot be explained by idleness.

Why it is not merely cosmetic: `Lww::join` (core/crdt.rs:38-49) orders on
`WriteStamp::wall_ms` FIRST (core/time.rs:44-49,148-151), so a fast-clocked host
wins merges it should lose. Same comparison drives note ordering
(core/state/notes.rs:97, core/bead.rs:764) and the delete-vs-recreate
resurrection rule. Partially absorbed by `Clock::tick` clamping forward jumps
past `hlc_max_forward_drift_ms` (default 600_000, core/limits.rs:131). So we DO
want real skew detection — we just don't currently have it in the positive
direction.

GUARD ALREADY IN PLACE: test `detect_clock_skew_positive_side_also_fires_on_a_
merely_idle_store` documents the current behaviour, so whoever changes it does
so deliberately and not by accident.
title: kopi-beans: clock_skew's POSITIVE branch is a staleness detector, not a skew detector (false positive on any idle store)
